facts.statement: The genus Archaeogaleus was described by Guinot, Cappetta, and Adnet in 2014.
The genus Archaeogaleus contains only one known species, A. lengadocensis.
facts.quote: It is known only from the species A. lengadocensis.

facts.statement: Archaeogaleus was first described from fossils found in the Valanginian stage of France.
facts.quote: It was described from the Valanginian stage of France.

facts.statement: The species name lengadocensis refers to the historical Occitan-speaking region of Lengadòc.
facts.quote: The specific epithet refers to Lengadòc, the region where Occitan was historically spoken.

facts.statement: Archaeogaleus is the oldest known requiem shark.
facts.quote: It is the oldest known requiem shark

facts.statement: Archaeogaleus belongs to the parent group Carcharhinidae.
Archaeogaleus is classified within the family Carcharhinidae.
Archaeogaleus is a member of the class Chondrichthyes.
Archaeogaleus lived during the Valanginian stage, between 137.05 and 132.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Valanginian (137.05 to 132.6 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Archaeogaleus likely had a dentition similar to the modern shark genus Scoliodon.
rejected.quote: It has a presumed dentition similar to the modern form Scoliodon.
